params.place: on the map: the tip of Russia facing Alaska across the Bering Strait

moments.what: a car rolls up to the tip of Russia, a road sign beside it pointing across the water
Russia's flag plants on its shore
the American flag plants on Alaska's shore and the sign's arrow lights
a dotted line arcs over the water
the camera pushes in on the waves between them

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: What if you could drive from Russia to Alaska, over the sea?

params.place: on the map: the Bering Strait, a ruler across its narrowest point

moments.what: the camera pulls up over the strait
BERING STRAIT writes on in the water
the two coasts light up
a ruler stretches from coast to coast
the width lands on the ruler's tag
the camera eases back to show both coasts whole

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: Here at the Bering Strait, only 82 kilometres of sea separate them.

params.place: on the map: the whole world from space, spinning until Russia and Alaska meet in the middle

moments.what: the camera pulls out to the whole flat world map
the map's edges outline
Russia lights on the right edge
Alaska lights on the left edge
the world spins east to west
the map keeps turning, oceans sliding past
Russia and Alaska slide together in the middle
the camera pushes in on the strait between them

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: On a flat world map, they sit at opposite edges. Spin the map around the globe, and they nearly touch.

params.place: on the map: the two Diomede islands in the middle of the strait

moments.what: the camera drifts to the middle of the strait
two islands pop up out of the sea
rings of surf circle them
BIG DIOMEDE writes on the larger island
a Russian flag plants on it
LITTLE DIOMEDE writes on the smaller island
an American flag plants on it

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: And right in the middle sit two islands: Big Diomede, which is Russian, and Little Diomede, which is American.

params.place: on the map: the narrow channel between the two islands, its depth marked

moments.what: a ruler stretches between the islands
the distance lands on its tag
the water turns see-through, showing the sea floor close below
a depth line drops into the water
the depth lands on a buoy's tag
a question mark pops over the channel
a dotted road line arcs from island to island
a red buoy bobs up in the channel
the depth line reaches the sea floor
the ruler's ends tick

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: They're just 3.8 kilometres apart, and the sea around them is only 90 metres at its deepest. So why not a road?

params.place: on the map: a bridge drawing itself across the strait, island to island

moments.what: a crane swings up on Russia's shore
the first span starts out over the water
it leaves Russia's coast
it lands on Big Diomede
a short span hops across the channel
it lands on Little Diomede
the last span runs east
it reaches Alaska and the whole bridge lights up
the three spans flash one after another
the two coasts light up together

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: So build it: one span from Russia to Big Diomede, a short hop to Little Diomede, and one more to Alaska. Three spans, and two continents are joined.

params.place: on the map: a road from London across Europe and Siberia, over the bridge to Alaska, Canada and New York

moments.what: the camera pulls far back over the top of the world
a car sets off from a pin on London
the road runs east across Europe
it runs on across Siberia, SIBERIA writing on
the car crosses the glowing bridge
it lands in Alaska
Canada fills with its flag as the road runs south-east
a pin drops on New York at the end of the road
a distance dial spins at the top

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: Now drive it. How far would that take you? From London, east across Europe, all through Siberia, over the bridge, then down through Alaska and Canada to New York.

params.place: on the map: the strait again, a planned tunnel drawn under the water

moments.what: a blueprint sheet with Russia's flag slides into the sky above the strait
a dashed tunnel line draws on the blueprint
the tunnel's dashed line drops under the water between the coasts
the tunnel's length lands on its tag
a price tag swings onto the plan
a red NEVER BUILT stamp hits the plan as the tunnel fades
the camera jolts closer on the stamped plan
a question mark pops over the strait
the tunnel line dips under the sea floor
the plan's paper flutters as the price is said
the blueprint's tunnel line pulses
the plan starts to grey

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: Has anyone tried? Russia backed a plan: a 103 kilometre tunnel under the strait, priced at about $65B. It was never built.

params.place: on the map: the date line running down the channel between the two islands

moments.what: the camera settles on the two islands
a dashed line draws down the sea from north to south
INTERNATIONAL DATE LINE writes on along it
calendar signs stand on both islands
a car rolls east across the bridge
the car crosses the line
the calendar on Little Diomede flips back a day
the camera eases back to show both islands
a clock on each calendar spins
both calendars pulse side by side

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: And the strangest part: the International Date Line runs between the two islands. Drive east from Big Diomede, and you arrive in yesterday. A short drive apart, but almost a whole day apart in time.

params.place: on the map: the strait with the bridge and the tunnel, then the tip of Russia facing Alaska again

moments.what: the bridge lights up across the strait
the dashed tunnel glows under the water
a question mark swings between them
both fade back
the car rolls up to the tip of Russia
Russia's coast lights
Alaska's coast lights as the frame settles on the hook's view

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: Bridge or tunnel: which would you build? Either way, you could drive from Russia to Alaska.

disclaimer: Maps simplified. Borders as recognised by the country each video is about.
